text:
Sam: heads-up — p95 for text-generation endpoints in eu-west jumped from ~90ms to ~420ms around 08:12 UTC after the maintenance window. Multiple customers complaining. graphs: https://grafana/redwood/eu-west/p95 (copy)
Priya: seeing same on embeddings pool, p95 and p99 both spiking. error rates are fine, just latency. :grimacing:
Miguel: any infra changes during the window? kernel/driver/firmware?
Sam: we applied kernel 6.7.x + nvidia 545.78 on the host pool at 08:05. Rollout to 25% then ramped. Canary looked ok initially.
Jordan: I started an iostat and dstat capture on an affected host — attaching snippet.
Jordan: ```
# iostat -x 1 20
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rsec/s wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.00 1.00 12.00 16.00 6144.00 512.00 8.40 120.5 10.1 122.9 2.00 98.0
``` 
Jordan: you can see big avgqu-sz spikes during the window.
Priya: also grabbing nvme-cli log: `nvme get-log --log-id=0x06` shows periodic flush events every ~10s.
Miguel: that smells like synchronous host flushes — maybe writeback/backpressure from the VM settings or a driver change that forces cache flushes.
Sam: repro plan idea: run a small fio workload to reproduce p95 locally while collecting nvme/blk stats.
Priya: trying fio on canary now with same kernel/driver. command:
Priya: ```
fio --name=randrw --rw=randrw --bs=16k --numjobs=8 --size=2G --runtime=120 --time_based --iodepth=32 --direct=1
```
Miguel: FYI we also saw elevated softirq times in the host kernel around the same timeframe. `cat /proc/softirqs` shows nvme-related irq spikes.
Jordan: quick mitigation suggestion: throttle background writeback so flushes don't produce big bursts. We can try tuning vm.dirty_* and the scheduler on a few canaries.
Sam: what exact sysctls? We need something quick to reduce p95 without risky rollback.
Priya: trying these on host-02 now (temporary):
Priya: ```
echo 50 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_ratio
echo 10 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_background_ratio
echo 150 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_expire_centisecs
echo 200 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_writeback_centisecs
```
Miguel: also set scheduler to mq-deadline: `echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler` — can smooth latency on mixed IO.
Jordan: applied the dirty_* tweaks on two affected hosts and routed 10% of traffic back. p95 dropped from ~420ms -> ~160ms on those hosts within 60s. :relieved:
Sam: good. Can we push this as immediate cluster mitigation to all affected hosts? Any risk to doing this cluster-wide?
Priya: risks: higher steady-state writeback means more background IO overall, potential throughput drop under heavy sustained writes. But for inference workload we're mostly read/prefetch + small writes for logs, seems acceptable short-term.
Miguel: alternative short-term: rollback nvidia driver to previous build on the smallest pool (10% of hosts) to see if regression is driver-related. But rollback is slower than sysctl tweak.
Sam: support asks for customer-facing mitigation — can we route heavy tail customers to dedicated capacity or enable smaller batch-size/low-latency profiles to reduce IO bursts?
Jordan: yes — traffic steering: enable low-batch routing rule for high-p95 orgs, fallback to CPU-backed small model instance if needed. I can flip routes in the next 10min.
Sam: action items:
Sam: 1) Priya apply sysctl tweaks to remaining affected hosts (in progress)
Sam: 2) Jordan create traffic steering rule to reduce batching for top 5 impacted customers
Sam: 3) Miguel run fio + nvme capture to reproduce and file a vendor driver bug if repro succeeds
Sam: 4) If sysctl doesn't fully resolve, plan rollback of nvidia driver for a small subset and measure
Priya: I'm on 1 now — will post results when done. ETA 15m.
Miguel: started fio now with `--output=fio-host02.log` and nvme logging. If we can reproduce flush every ~10s and see corresponding latency spike, that'll be a strong signal.
Priya: sysctl applied to 6 hosts. p95 cluster-wide dropped from 420ms -> 180ms. p99 still high but improving.
Jordan: traffic steer in place for top 3 customers — reducing burstiness and aborts for some. Notifying support.
Sam: Miguel — if driver is root cause we need an RCA timeline. Please open a ticket with vendor with attached traces, fio repro, nvme logs. Mark priority P1.
Miguel: opened internal issue INF-7122 and vendor ticket with logs attached. Message: reproducible p95 spike linked to periodic nvme flushes after kernel 6.7 + nvidia 545.78. Link: https://redwood/issue/INF-7122
Priya: for longer term, we should add a preflight perf check for storage flush patterns in rollout pipeline and add a canary workload that triggers small random IO to catch this earlier.
Sam: agreed. Also add an automatic mitigation playbook entry for 'hostfs flush storm' with the sysctl knobs and traffic-steering runbook.
Jordan: I'll draft the postmortem once this stabilizes. For now, monitoring alert updated to include nvme avgq and dirty_writeback metrics.
infra-bot: deploy rollback patch queued for test pool (can't execute without 2 approvals)
Sam: thanks everyone. I'll update support and customers with the mitigation steps and ETA for RCA.
Priya: final note — keep an eye on sustained background IO after sysctl change; revert if we see degradation in throughput.
